title: Memorization Is Folding: Topological Signatures of Noisy-Label Learning
claim: Corruption leaves a measurable geometric signature that emerges with training and depends on the persistence metric used, not on label fitting.
layout: 2 side-by-side dot plots, left-to-right, dashed baseline at ratio one
description: Two scatter-style panels share a white background and use dashed gray reference lines at a ratio of one. Panel (a) plots corrupted/clean persistence ratios (Φ_H1/Φ_H0, log axis) against training epochs 10, 25 and 50. At each epoch, blue circles (sf=0.25) and orange squares (sf=0.5) show per-seed dots, and a thick black bar marks each group's median. The medians sit near 1 at epoch 10 and climb to about 1.25 by epoch 50. Panel (b) compares random/Patrini ratios at epoch 50 for two metrics. Mean activation norm sits below 1, near 0.7, in gray and is labeled '0/8 > 1'. Cosine persistence sits near 2.7, in black, and is labeled '8/8 > 1'. The eye goes first to the separated cluster in (b) and the rising medians in (a).
caption: Seed-level persistence comparisons. (a) Corrupted/clean ratios of ΦH1/ΦH0 on the fixed CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 training probe, with eight seeds per setting. Dots show within-run ratios and horizontal bars show their medians. These differ from the ratios of seed medians reported in Table 2. (b) Epoch-50 random/Patrini ratios for mean activation norm and cosine persistence. Each dot shows one seed’s median ratio across three nominal settings. The random arm changes approximately 1.8 times as many labels as the Patrini arm, so the comparison includes differences in both corruption rate and relabelling structure. Both panels use logarithmic vertical axes. Dashed lines mark a ratio of one.
abstract: How does noisy supervision change the representations learned by a neural network? Training accuracy measures agreement with training labels but provides little information about representation geometry. We use persistent homology to track loop structure across distance thresholds in neural activations. Experiments span image classification, text classification, and modular arithmetic. On a fixed CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 training probe, equally sized clean-label and corrupted-label subsets show no detectable persistence difference at epoch 10, whereas corrupted-label subsets have higher persistence at epoch 50. The contrast survives uniform-scale controls, even though predictions match the assigned noisy labels for only 7–11% of corrupted probe examples at that checkpoint. Normalisation preserves the crossover between clean and noisy training trajectories on CIFAR-10/ResNet-18, whereas CIFAR-100/ResNet-18 shows no crossover under any of the five evaluated constructions. In a separate noise-rate calibration comparison across five pipelines, mean activation norm achieves a higher mean in-sample R² than raw persistence (0.936 versus 0.908). These findings show that noisy supervision leaves a measurable geometric signature even when agreement with corrupted labels is low. Tracking scale-controlled persistence alongside label fitting offers a way to study how networks reorganise their internal representations during training. This provides a basis for developing training diagnostics that complement accuracy.
